“One Minutes” (15 per side)

Senate Amendments to H.R. 5334 – Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (Rep. Panetta – Foreign Affairs) (Subject to a Rule)

This legislation authorizes a raft of sanctions against Russian leaders, companies, and their enablers, and additionally grants President Trump broad new tariff authorities to be used on any country he chooses. In addition, the legislation includes very broad waiver authority to be used at the president’s discretion.

House Democrats have remained steadfast supporters of Ukraine as it fights against Russia’s ruthless invasion. From securing investment increases for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative to leading a successful discharge petition to bring the Ukraine Support Act to the Floor, House Democrats have and will continue to stand by Ukraine and up to Russia – for the freedom of Ukraine, the national security of America, and the safety of countries across the globe.

Meanwhile, President Trump has shown time and time again that he is unwilling to take a stand against Russia and President Putin. He has consistently refused to impose or enforce tough sanctions on Russia and constantly threatens the ability of Ukraine to defend itself from Russian aggression. The sanctions in this legislation are optional because of the waiver authority and the bill provides no reconstruction or security assistance to Ukraine. Given President Trump’s terrible track record on Ukraine, there is no reason to think he will use the authorities in this bill to pressure President Putin.

This package is also handing President Trump sweeping tariff authority to continue his erratic and unjustified tariff regime. The world has just witnessed an unprecedented tariff assault on Canada, our closest ally, because President Trump was mad that Canada stood up to him for imposing illegal tariffs. President Trump’s tariffs are already costing American households over $1,000 per year, forcing families to stretch every dollar. This bill could make that even harder by driving prices up even further. Depending on the whims of an erratic president, Ways and Means Democrats estimate that this bill could add an additional $8,000 or more to the tariff costs crippling American consumers.

As Americans continue to suffer from the cost-of-living crisis – due in no small part to the president’s tariffs – this package would grant the Trump Administration even greater power to wreak havoc on the lives of everyday Americans and the global economy. This is not a sanctions bill, but rather a tariff bill with some discretionary sanctions thrown in that President Trump has no interest in applying.

Ranking Members Meeks and Neal strongly oppose this bill.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Foreign Affairs or their respective designees.

H.R. 9576 – National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026 (Rep. Finstad – Judiciary) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill codifies the creation of a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice, as well as the appointed position of Assistant Attorney General for National Fraud Enforcement. The Trump Administration created this Division through regulation earlier this year.

Fighting fraud is important, but this bill fails to define any mission for the new National Fraud Enforcement Division – a creation of the most pro-fraud administration in American history. In fact, the amended text that House Republicans will bring to the Floor strips the original bill of any obligation for the Fraud Division to fight fraud.

House Democrats are ready to work on real solutions so that critical government programs are protected against fraud – from those both inside and outside the White House.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on the Judiciary or their respective designees.

H.R. 10326 – Preventing Rip-offs and Obtaining Oversight of Funds Act (Rep. Van Drew – Judiciary) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill requires states to provide the Attorney General with the private data of any American enrolled in a federally funded, state-administered program. This bill is not about “fighting fraud.” In this administration and every administration before it, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has already brought fraud cases using the available tools to obtain information for legitimate investigative purposes. 

In reality, this bill is about destroying the statutory privacy protections governing each of these programs for Americans and allowing DOJ to build the Big Brother database containing Americans’ personal, private information that DOGE and this administration have been trying to build from Day One. These efforts have been blocked by court orders in several lawsuits. 

This sweeping bill has not gone through regular order – it has had no hearing or markup in the House Judiciary Committee. Instead, House Republicans are trying to rush it to the Floor and pass it at the last-minute, hoping the American people won’t see it. 

Ranking Member Raskin strongly opposes this bill.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on the Judiciary or their respective designees.

H.J.Res. 213 – Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the ‘‘California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision’’ (Rep. Gallagher – Energy and Commerce) (Subject to a Rule) – VOTE NO

This resolution seeks to overturn the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) notices of decision that grant waivers of federal preemption under the Clean Air Act (CAA) to California’s Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth standards. Specifically, H.J.Res. 213 goes after the latest Commercial Harbor Craft rule, which requires cleaner engines on commercial harbor craft vessels – including excursion vessels, tugboats, ferries, pilot boats, research vessels, and commercial fishing barges – that operate within California waters.

Notably, this rule helps vessels cut or eliminate the use of expensive and dirty diesel fuel while on the water or docked. These House Republican resolutions would overturn those protections, forcing vessels to burn more diesel fuel at a moment when prices are at a record high of over $6 nationally, driving up costs for American families.

Right now, Americans across the country are facing an affordability crisis caused by the disastrous decisions of the Trump Administration. Between President Trump’s war of choice with Iran and erratic tariff regime, inflation remains high and the costs of gas, groceries, and more continue to soar. Throughout all this, House Republicans have refused to stand up to the administration and continue to erode Congressional authority. Now they are willing to take a stand – against rules to protect Americans from health-harming pollution and the soaring cost of diesel fuel, all to line the pockets of their corporate polluter friends.

As a reminder, any joint resolution of disapproval that qualifies under the CRA has the force of law and prohibits agencies from issuing any rules that are “substantially the same” in the future. Republicans and EPA are, once again, abusing the CRA to retroactively target long-standing, legally authorized CAA waivers. GAO and the Senate Parliamentarian concluded these waivers are not “rules” subject to the CRA – and this week a court agreed, blocking EPA from reclassifying CAA waivers as rules. Yet, House Republicans are ignoring the law and forging ahead with this illegal disapproval resolution.

Ranking Member Pallone strongly opposes this resolution.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Energy and Commerce or their respective designees.

Complete Consideration of H.Con.Res. 93 – Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (Rep. Moulton – Foreign Affairs) (Privileged Resolution) – VOTE YES

This resolution would direct the president to terminate the use of the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran unless authorized by a formal declaration of war or an authorization for the use of military force. It has no impact on the presence of U.S. Armed Forces in the region or the gathering and sharing of intelligence and counterintelligence and explicitly allows U.S. forces to defend themselves, partners, or allies from imminent attack. It is the exact text of H.Con.Res. 86, which passed the House with all Democrats in support. 

President Trump continues to endanger our brave men and women in uniform without making the case to the public or Congress for this costly and unconstitutional war of choice. Now over six months in, the administration has spent tens of billions of dollars on this war with no true end in sight – all while making false promises to the American public. Meanwhile, the price of diesel just reached over $6 a gallon, setting a new record. Americans simply cannot afford for this war to go on as it continues to put upward pressure on prices both at the pump and the grocery store.

Despite all this, House Republicans continue to make excuses for the president and keep Congress on the sidelines while the President illegally starts and stops the war powers clock. If they were truly serious about helping working- and middle-class Americans – who are struggling to afford healthcare, rent, groceries, gas, and more – make ends meet, more House Republicans would join House Democrats in ending a conflict that has injured over 800 brave men and women in uniform and cost the lives of 18 courageous service members.

Ranking Member Meeks strongly supports this resolution.

H.R. 4795 – Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act (Rep. Foxx – Education and Workforce) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill would prevent institutions of higher education (IHEs) from accessing Title IV Higher Education Act (HEA) funds if they are engaged in a “nonexpressive commercial boycott” of Israel. Under the bill, a “nonexpressive commercial boycott” is defined as a commercial action – such as terminating business activities – intended to limit commercial relations and is not based on a valid business reason. Under the bill’s definition there are currently no IHEs engaged in a nonexpressive commercial boycott of Israel. Additionally, the bill would require IHEs to certify that students are permitted to participate in academic programs and cultural exchanges with Israel in order to access international education funding under the HEA.

The Rule, which was adopted on Tuesday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Education and Workforce or their respective designees.
